raw_response:
I have farmed this land a long time, so I do not change too much unless I have a reason. On my 10.1 mu, wheat-maize rotation is still the safest way for me. It spreads risk and keeps the land working the whole year. I have well water, so I am not fully dependent on rain, but pumping costs money, and with only 2 people in the household and some off-farm work, I cannot manage something too labor-intensive. Since my education is relatively high, I do look at crop condition, soil strength, and last year's yield when I decide fertilizer, but I still follow what has worked on my own fields. For wheat, I will stay with an improved local variety, sow on time in October, use base fertilizer plus one topdressing, and irrigate at the key stages instead of too many times. For summer maize, the turnaround after wheat is very tight, so I will keep tillage simple, use a hybrid seed, and put more attention on getting it planted quickly after wheat harvest. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer and timely irrigation than risk a weak stand, but I still need to keep cash in hand, so I am not pushing inputs to the maximum.
